rule.title: Mixed conditionals
rule.explanation:
Los condicionales mixtos combinan tiempos cuando la causa y la consecuencia están en momentos distintos:
- Pasado → presente: «If» + past perfect, «would» + verbo. Algo que pasó (o no) tiene una consecuencia ahora: «If I hadn't taken that job, I wouldn't be here now.»
- Presente (rasgo general) → pasado: «If» + past simple, «would have» + participio. Cómo somos explica algo que pasó: «If I weren't so lazy, I would have passed the first time.»

Más ejemplos:
- «If we hadn't met, I wouldn't be so happy now.»
- «If she spoke Spanish, she would have understood the joke.»

Recuerda los tipos puros para compararlos: el segundo condicional va de presente a presente («If I had money, I'd buy it») y el tercero, de pasado a pasado («If I had had money, I would have bought it»).

Ojo: la contracción «'d» después de «if» es «had»; delante de un verbo, «would»: «If I'd stayed (had), I'd be (would) bored now».

rows: If I'd studied, I'd have a better job now.
If + past simple, would have + participio
If I were braver, I'd have asked her.
If I had time, I'd help.
If + past perfect, would have + participio
If I'd known, I'd have come.
